sb_prompt: WHY DO YOU THINK THAT ONLY ABOUT HALF OF ELIGIBLE VOTERS IN AMERICA TAKE PART IN NATIONAL ELECTIONS
turns: Yeah, I've been wondering about that too. My cousin is in that demographic and she's just so passionate about it, yet she says people like her just don't get out.
Yeah, that's what I'm trying to figure out too, honestly. I've been thinking about it for years, just never quite knew why.
Yeah, my cousin actually called me last week and she was getting really upset because she thinks it's personal, like we just don't care enough, but I felt like maybe there's more to it than that.
Yeah, I mean, I've been in this business for a while and I see people walk right past the polls every single day. It's like they just aren't seeing it as their responsibility.
I get that you see it as a responsibility, but honestly, my cousin's just so overwhelmed by everything else going on in her life that it feels like too much of a hassle.
Yeah, but I still don't get why she doesn't try to make time.
I mean, she works full time, has three kids, and honestly, driving her to the register and waiting in line feels like too much stress when she's already burned out by the end of the day.
Yeah, but you can't just show up at the polls if your kids are sick and your boss needs you in the office.

I get that, but then why are the polls so hard to get to? My cousin lives only twenty minutes away, yet she says the traffic is just unbearable on election day and she can't even leave work early enough.
Yeah, but my cousin is eligible, so why can't she just take a day off?
Well, she's got a boss who wouldn't let her off, but honestly, I think the main thing is that she just feels like her vote doesn't actually matter anymore.
Yeah, but that's exactly what I don't understand, because I've always felt like my vote mattered more than ever.
But that's not the point, is it? It's not about me taking the day off, it's about the whole system being set up in a way that makes people feel like they can't actually make it happen.
Yeah, but I still think if she just made it a priority, she'd find a way.
But making it a priority doesn't help if you're stuck in traffic for two hours because the polls aren't open early enough.
I guess you're right, but I still can't shake the feeling that she's just choosing not to show up.
She's been through a divorce and she's barely holding on, so asking her to battle through lines and traffic feels like setting her up to fail rather than helping her do her duty.
I don't know, it just sounds like an excuse to me.
It's not an excuse, it's the reality that when you're drowning, the last thing you have the energy to do is fight a bureaucratic war.
I just don't see how it's an excuse if the roads aren't closed down.
And roads aren't closed, but sometimes when you're exhausted, even a short trip feels like climbing a mountain.
That makes sense, but still... how is she supposed to get it done then?
She doesn't even have the energy to look up the address beforehand, let alone drive there.
I mean, if she just looked up the address, maybe it wouldn't feel so hard.
Look, if she's already searching for the address, she's barely got the energy to look for it.
I mean, at least she could ask someone to drive her if she's that tired.
She's not asking for someone to drive her; she's too broken down to even speak to another person about it right now.
Yeah, but if she's that overwhelmed, asking her to ask someone else feels like too much work too.
Yeah, but asking her to ask someone else feels like a hurdle she literally can't climb right now.
Yeah, but asking someone else feels like too much work if you're already at your limit.
Yeah, but if she's at her limit, asking for help feels like throwing sand in the gears of something already grinding to a halt.
Yeah, I guess you're right, but still... how is she supposed to get it done then?
She can't just conjure up the energy to fight through it without the system making it a little easier to access.
I mean, I still don't buy that she's truly powerless to change it though.
She's not powerless, she's just exhausted to the point where even the idea of fighting feels like too heavy a weight to carry.
Yeah, but I still don't know why she just won't try.
Because if the system isn't set up to meet people where they're at, they just fall by the wayside.
I mean, if she falls by the wayside, then what is the point of being eligible in the first place?
Then maybe the system needs to be different so people don't have to fight just to be heard.
